events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Giessen to a Hessian public official's family.

evidence.quote: Wilhelm Liebknecht was born in 1826 in Giessen
( 29 March 1826 – 7 August 1900 )

events.text: Began schooling at the Gymnasium of Giessen.

evidence.quote: From 1832 to 1842 , he went to school at the Gymnasium of Giessen

events.text: Ended schooling at the Gymnasium of Giessen.

evidence.quote: From 1832 to 1842 , he went to school at the Gymnasium of Giessen

events.text: Found himself in Switzerland during its civil war.

evidence.quote: Thus he found himself in Switzerland in 1847

events.text: Hurried to Paris as the February 1848 revolution erupted.

evidence.quote: When revolution erupted in Paris in February 1848 , Liebknecht hurried to the scene

events.label: arrest
events.text: Arrested in Switzerland for uniting German workers' associations and banished.

evidence.quote: In 1850 , Liebknecht was arrested for his initiatives to unite Switzerlands German workers associations and was banished from the country

events.text: Relocated his exile to London, where he stayed until 1862.

evidence.quote: he relocated his exile to London , where he stayed from 1850 to 1862

events.text: Returned to Germany after the amnesty for 1848 revolution participants.

evidence.quote: In 1862 , after an amnesty for the participants in the revolution of 1848 , he returned to Germany

events.text: Became a member of Lassalle's General German Workers Association (ADAV).

evidence.quote: In 1862 , after an amnesty for the participants in the revolution of 1848 , he returned to Germany and became a member of
Ferdinand Lassalles General German Workers Association ( Allgemeiner Deutscher Arbeiterverein , ADAV )

events.text: Began working for the magazine Der Social-Demokrat.

evidence.quote: From 1864 to 1865 , Liebknecht also worked for the magazine Der Social-Demokrat

events.text: Ended work for Der Social-Demokrat and quit its editorial staff.

evidence.quote: From 1864 to 1865 , Liebknecht also worked for the magazine Der Social-Demokrat

events.text: Co-founded the Saxon Peoples Party with August Bebel.

evidence.quote: with whom he founded the Sächsische Volkspartei ( Saxon Peoples Party ) in 1867

events.text: Co-founded the Social Democratic Workers Party of Germany (SDAP) in Eisenach.

evidence.quote: and the Social Democratic Workers Party of Germany ( Sozialdemokratische Arbeiterpartei Deutschlands , SDAP ) in 1869 in Eisenach

events.label: anti-war agitation
events.text: Used his newspaper to agitate against the Franco-Prussian War.

evidence.quote: When the Franco-Prussian War began in 1870 , Liebknecht used his newspaper to agitate against the war

events.label: conviction
events.text: Convicted of treason with Bebel and sentenced to two years' fortress imprisonment.

evidence.quote: In 1872 , both Liebknecht and Bebel were convicted and sentenced to two years of

events.text: Re-elected to the Reichstag.

evidence.quote: After being re-elected to the Reichstag in 1874

events.text: Helped merge the SDAP and ADAV into the SAPD at Gotha.

evidence.quote: ( Sozialistische Arbeiterpartei Deutschlands , SAPD ) in Gotha in 1875

events.text: Published the book Zur Grund- und Bodenfrage in Leipzig.

evidence.quote: Zur Grund- und Bodenfrage , Leipzig , 1876

events.text: Published the book Ein Blick in die Neue Welt in Stuttgart.

evidence.quote: Ein Blick in die Neue Welt , Stuttgart , 1887

events.text: Became editor-in-chief of the party newspaper Vorwärts.

evidence.quote: In 1891 , Liebknecht became editor-in-chief of Vorwärts

events.text: Helped originate the SPD's new Marxist-inspired party platform.

evidence.quote: In 1891 , Liebknecht became editor-in-chief of Vorwärts and one of the originators of the SPDs new Marxist-inspired party platform

events.text: Published the book Robert Owen: Sein Leben und sozialpolitischen Wirken.

events.label: death
events.text: Died aged 74 in Charlottenburg, a suburb of Berlin.

evidence.quote: Liebknecht died aged 74 on 7 August 1900 in Charlottenburg
( 29 March 1826 – 7 August 1900 )

events.text: Published the book Karl Marx: Biographical Memoirs in Chicago.

evidence.quote: Karl Marx : Biographical Memoirs , Chicago , 1906

undated_mentions: Decided to emigrate to the United States after trouble over student radicalism in Giessen
Studied philology, theology and philosophy in Giessen, Berlin and Marburg
Took an unpaid teaching post at a progressive school in Zurich
Began journalism career reporting Swiss civil war for the Mannheimer Abendzeitung
Joined a legion travelling to Germany; arrested in Baden and charged with treason; released by a mob
Member of the Badische Volkswehr, adjutant of Gustav von Struve, fought in the Reichsverfassungskämpfe
Escaped to Switzerland and became a leading member of the Genfer Arbeiterverein; met Friedrich Engels
Became a member of the Communist League in London
Developed a lifelong friendship and collaboration with Karl Marx in London
Evicted from Berlin, moved to Leipzig and met August Bebel
Forced to leave the ADAV under pressure from Schweitzer
Elected to the national legislature and opposed Bismarck's policies (late 1860s)
Editor of the party newspaper Der Volksstaat
Arrested and charged with treason with Bebel after anti-war agitation (c. 1870-71)
Became publisher of the newly founded party organ Vorwärts (after 1875)
Continued to serve in the Reichstag throughout the 1890s
Major organizer of the Second Socialist International
